p:cNvPr.descr: A model illustrating the synthesis of N-acetylglutamate ad its action of carbamoyl phosphate synthetase I. At the top is acetyl-CoA, where C bonds left to CH3, double bonds up and right to O, and bonds down and right to S-CoA. To the right is a plus sign. Right of that is glutamate, where C bonds left to H3N (plus sign over N), up to COO-, right to H, and down to CH2, which bonds down to CH2, which bonds down to COO-. Below this is an arrow pointing down to N-acetylglutamate, represented as N-acetylglutamate synthase (in blue). To the right of the arrow is a green triangle in a circle, with arginine to the right. This arrow also has another arrow jetting off to CoA-SH. N-acetylglutamate begins with C, which bonds left to CH3, double bonds up to O, and bonds right to NH, which bonds right to C. C bonds up to COO-, right to H, and down to CH2, which bonds down to CH2, which bonds down to COO-. Below this, is HCO3- [plus] NH4+. To the right is an arrow, represented as carbamoyl phosphate synthetase I (in blue), pointing to carbamoyl phosphate. Above that is a curved arrow from 2ATP to 2ADP [plus] Pi. In the middle of the curved arrow is a green triangle in a circle. Carbamoyl phosphate begins with C, which bonds left to H2N, double bonds up to O, and bonds right to O, which bonds right to P. P double bonds up to O, bonds right to O- and down to O-.
